title: Every ranked model reports in a ranked unit
how: Models of kind charity with an output that aren't side sheets (what rankingPlan can pick) must have output.unit in {uov, daly, wellby, ced, tco2e}.

title: Headline = native result × the unit's conversion × the estimate's age factor × an import's missing-data factor (our view)
how: headline(m) in the charityevals view against compute(m)[output] × evaluate(headlineConversion(unit)) × (1 + $estimate_age_discount)^−age, age from source.published to common.estimate_age_as_of (2.11), × an imported model's missing-data factor 1 − thin_share × (1 − $missing_data_discount) (2.12, INV-21); and bottomLine(m).common, what `#id` and the rankings read, against the headline × $uov_per_daly / 1000. The evaluator view is INV-8 (no age factor). Whether each unit's conversion is the standard recipe is INV-1 (sad and animals_spared have no standard recipe).

title: No model row reads a cross-cause rate
how: Every row a model wrote itself (variants: only rows they override): assumptionDeps ∩ {$daly_per_sad, $daly_per_wellby, $sads_per_animal_spared, $chicken_vs_person, $daly_per_disabling_day, $deaths_per_tco2e, $climate_heat_share, $climate_heat_death_delay} must be empty, and $uov_per_daly only where evaluator.assumptions pins it. Bridges are exempt (docs/normalization.md 2.6): a row in an ours section whose formula is exactly <input> * (<to_common of a ranked unit>) / (<to_common of the output unit>), which the output unit's conversion cancels, so the outcome in <input> reaches the headline through its own unit's shared conversion; WELLBY models' wellbys_from_uov = uov_valued_outside_wellbys / ($daly_per_wellby * $uov_per_daly) is the bridge from uov (INV-17), and what it converts reads no WELLBY rate. Rows a bridge reads besides its input (a tco2e bridge's air_pollution_weight) are held to the conversion-row rule below. The one sanctioned way a model shapes its conversion is a row the unit's to_common names by a fixed id (tco2e: air_pollution_weight, docs/normalization.md 2.5): it must sit in an ours section, and neither it nor any row feeding it may read a shared assumption.

title: No evaluator's own conversion in our view
how: Every input row on the path to the output (variants: their overrides) whose id and label name one of 6 kinds of conversion (exchange rate between outcomes; value of a death; depression scale to health; cash benchmark; exchange rate between currencies; discount rate), and every read of a fact holding an evaluator's own conversion (@founders_pledge.wellbys_per_daly, @founders_pledge.wellbys_per_doubling, @founders_pledge.gd_cost_per_wellby), is moved ×1.25 in our view: the headline must not move. A literal that matters is the evaluator's own conversion: the row must read the shared fact or assumption, with the evaluator's figure in `published` (rows reading a shared value are formulas, so they aren't candidates). Heuristic on labels: a conversion under other words isn't seen, and a flagged row that isn't a conversion gets a waiver with its reason.

title: No literal times a lever
how: Every formula row on the path to the output (variants: their overrides) is split into its product and quotient chains and its function calls' argument lists; a chain or argument list holding both a non-toggle shared assumption ($life_value_multiplier, $discount_rate, …) and a constant outside lint's ALLOWED_LITERALS (0, 1, 0.5, 100, 1000, 100000, 1000000, 12, 52, 365, 365.25, 0.000001) is flagged. Such a constant is a value the lever is meant to replace (8 for a death next to $life_value_multiplier) or an evaluator's input that INV-2c, INV-4 and INV-13 can't see inside a formula: it must read the shared fact, with the evaluator's figure in `published`, or become its own labelled input row. ln(2) and other constants inside a function of their own (not beside the assumption) pass.

title: Every animal model passes through the species step, once per species, from the shared table
how: Animal models must report in ced and declare output.species. For each species s there is a row ced_<s> whose formula equals the standard template (AIM SADs: sads_<s> / @aim_sads.<s>_<v> * if($rp_species_weights, @welfare_ranges.<s>_vs_chicken, @aim_sads.<s>_<v> / @aim_sads.chicken_2024), v the SAD version, 2024 or 2025, whose weight is built into the figure; a second version for the same species goes in ced_<s>_<v> on sads_<s>_<v>; raw days: pain_days_<s> * @welfare_ranges.<s>_vs_chicken) up to whitespace, reads @welfare_ranges.<s>_vs_chicken and feeds the output. No other row reads @welfare_ranges.* or @aim_sads.*. Not checked: that every path from a SAD or pain-day row to the output passes through a ced_* row (rows carry no unit to tell).

title: No literal stands in for a shared fact or assumption
how: Facts have no `match` pattern yet, so (a) an input row is flagged when its value equals a fact's or assumption's low/best/high (within 0.2%) AND its id+label shares at least two significant words (half the smaller label) with the fact's label, or uses one of the synonyms for it (ln(consumption) or a doubled income for $uov_per_ln_consumption; a DALY or disability weight or (DW) for the GBD weights; GiveDirectly's cost-effectiveness or a cash benchmark for @cash); near-equal (not equal) values without a synonym, one-significant-digit values (0.5, 1000) and facts with generic labels ("Average household size") need closer labels (50%, 60%, 75% of the larger word set); a country fact (givewell_kenya…) only matches rows naming that country; (b) a formula constant outside lint's ALLOWED_LITERALS is flagged when it equals a fact's or assumption's best value exactly and either has 5+ significant digits and isn't an integer (116.25262, 73.1914) or the row label resembles the shared label. Rows a model wrote itself only (variants: overrides). The evaluator's own number is still a violation: it belongs in `published` on a row that reads the fact. Heuristic by nature (values and words, not meaning); it can't see a copy whose label uses other words ("CFR" for case fatality rate), a copy rounded beyond 0.1% or rescaled (a percent written as 12, a rate per 1,000), a short formula constant under an unlike label, a shared number that isn't in facts/ or assumptions yet, or a country fact for a place outside its list; and a matching label can still be a coincidence (normalization-waivers.json).

title: The evaluator view uses the evaluator's own rates
how: Every evaluator model with an output (variants too, with their own inputs) must declare output.native; its evaluator layer is the native row, every row feeding it and every other row outside sections of kind "ours". Each non-toggle assumption a row in that layer reads is moved to ×0.5 and ×1.5 in our view (0 → 0.5 and 1): no row of the layer may move in the evaluator view, so every `expected` still reproduces and the bottom line stays the evaluator's. A pin in evaluator.assumptions passes by construction; an unpinned assumption passes only if no evaluator row's value depends on it. Each toggle the layer reads (GiveWell's leverage and funging switches on $resource_shares) must be pinned, so the evaluator view sees the evaluator's position.

title: The evaluator's bottom line reproduces
how: Every evaluator model with an output (not variants: they inherit output.native and don't inherit `expected`) declares output.native, and that row or one of its direct inputs carries `expected`; scripts/check.ts checks those values reproduce in the evaluator view.

title: Our rows are visibly ours
how: Every evaluator model with an output (not variants: rows and sections are the parent's) declares output.native, and the output uses it. The output uses the native row (or, for a result split by species, every direct input of it). Every row that feeds the output and is computed, directly or not, from the native row or one of its direct inputs (without feeding the native row itself) is in a section of kind "ours" and has no `expected`; no row in the layer is in one of ours (rows switched by a toggle inside the evaluator's layer stay the evaluator's: INV-5 checks the toggle is pinned). Not checked: inputs of our steps that aren't computed from the bottom line (GiveWell's value of cash, staff-pay judgments; ours by section), and evaluator rows beside the bottom line that a bridge reads (ACE 2016's hen-years; INV-5 still holds them to the evaluator's rates).

title: One view, one set of numbers
how: headline(m, av, {}, "evaluator") against compute(evaluator view)[output] × the unit's conversion evaluated with viewAssumptions(m, av, "evaluator"). Fails wherever a pin changes a rate in the conversion ($uov_per_daly for uov models).

title: Shared levers reach every model they apply to
how: Models don't declare mortality/multi_year yet, so keywords in the labels of rows on the path to the output stand in: deaths/mortality/lives saved (not seedlings, trees, crops) → some row on the path must read $life_value_multiplier; discount rate/factor, present value, years or duration of benefit/effect, decay (not iron absorption discount factors) → some row on the path must read $discount_rate. Variants are checked through their parent. Heuristic by nature (keywords, not declarations); it can't see deaths valued under another name (DALYs or years of life lost, "lives" without "saved"), benefits spread over years without the keywords, or a lever read on one branch of the path while another branch values deaths or years with literals; and it flags sheets where the words are context only (normalization-waivers.json).

title: Benefits over several years are discounted
how: Every input row on the path to the output (variants: their overrides) whose label counts how long a benefit, change, coverage or flow of money lasts (years of change/impact/benefit/production/funding, number of years, duration of the effect) and is above 1 is moved ×1.25 in our view, once at a 0% discount rate and once at max(8%, twice the default): if the headline rises, and by the same factor at both rates, those years are added up at face value and must be discounted at $discount_rate. Heuristic on labels: years counted under other words aren't seen, and a frozen present value (a cached PV typed in as a number) isn't either.

title: Every evaluator pin is read
how: For every model with evaluator.assumptions, each pinned assumption must be read by some row of the model (inherited rows count) or by its output unit's conversion. An unread pin is either a lever the model should read (a death valued without $life_value_multiplier, years without $discount_rate) or dead weight to drop.

title: Each slider moves exactly the models it should
how: At the defaults, each headline is recomputed with one assumption ×1.5 (and ×0.5 for linearity). Animal models: proportional to $chicken_vs_person and $daly_per_sad (the design's $daly_per_disabling_day), independent of $uov_per_daly, $daly_per_wellby, $uov_per_ln_consumption. Climate (tco2e) models: proportional to $deaths_per_tco2e and $life_value_multiplier, independent of the animal assumptions, $daly_per_wellby and $uov_per_ln_consumption. Others: independent of the animal assumptions, $deaths_per_tco2e, $climate_heat_death_delay and $daly_per_wellby, except WELLBY models, which are proportional to $daly_per_wellby and independent of $uov_per_daly and $uov_per_ln_consumption (with the deaths they value outside their WELLBYs, uov_valued_outside_wellbys, held at 0: INV-17 checks those). Every bridge's input (docs/normalization.md 2.6) is held at 0 for the output unit's expectations, and the part it brings in (headline − headline with the input at 0) must move as a model of its own unit would (a uov part independent of the animal, WELLBY and climate rates; a ced part proportional to the animal ones). Models with a zero or non-finite headline are skipped. A model that reads other models live (`#id`) is not expected to be independent of an assumption those models read.

title: Same physical change, same SADs figure
how: Rows in animal models whose label states SADs per unit for one of 5 transitions (hen-battery-to-cage-free, hen-enriched-to-cage-free, broiler-bcc, meal-replaced, shrimp-stunned), matched by label keywords (the explainer only tells battery from enriched cages). Each must read its shared fact in facts/sad_factors.json; shrimp stunning has no fact yet, so every shrimp-stunned row fails while the models disagree. Not matched: "animals spared → SADs" and "years of farmed life → SADs" ratios (Good Food Fund's $sads_per_animal_spared, ACE 2016's caged-hen 28.9 per year), which are spread over formulas and are a different quantity from a transition; per-dollar rows (the species step's sads_<s> split, "SADs per dollar you give: chickens") and shares of SADs by species or SAD version, which are results, not a transition's figure.

title: No evaluator-internal exchange rate where a shared one exists
how: Every model, charityevals' own included (since 2026-11-03; every evaluator's since 2026-11-02, before that Ambitious Impact's only): every row on the path to the output whose label states an income-to-health exchange rate (years of doubled consumption to DALYs); a value of a death averted, in DALYs or years of life; a value of a stillbirth averted; a pound or euro exchange rate must read the shared version ($uov_per_ln_consumption (and $uov_per_daly); @moral_weights.* * $life_value_multiplier; @givewell_shared.uov_per_stillbirth * $life_value_multiplier / $uov_per_daly; @fx.*). Labels stand in for meaning, so a rate under another name isn't seen.

title: Money moved and career changes are valued one way
how: Every model (not variants) whose native unit or a row on the path to the output names money moved, raised, influenced, affected or shifted, a leverage ratio, a gross multiplier or EA donations must reach its output through the shared row moved_dollar_value, with the shared formula (destinations across causes, or global health only); every shared row it has (value_global_health, value_livelihoods, value_tlycs_recommended, prior_dollar_value, new_money_share, moved_dollar_net_value) must have the shared formula word for word; and every row on its path stating an organisation's chance of success must read @meta.success_chance_new_org. A row on the path about career changes needs the shared career_change_value = career_forgone_pay * career_years * career_employer_value * career_counterfactual_share. Labels stand in for meaning, so money moved under other words isn't seen, and a charity's own fundraising or a funder's value-of-information sheet is waived with its reason.

title: Same concept, same value across models
how: Rows on the path to the output (not variants) whose label names one of 19 concepts several evaluators state (resource-sharing, treatment-costs-averted, investment-of-income, long-term-benefit-years, wage-gain-per-iq-point, cf-value-government, cf-value-global-fund, cf-value-gavi, income-to-mortality-ratio, value-of-cyp, value-of-stillbirth, indirect-deaths-malaria, malaria-morbidity, indirect-deaths-diarrhea, household-spillover-therapy, household-size, commitment-fulfilment, prior-weight-education, depression-per-phq9-point) must read the concept's shared fact (or be computed from a row that does), with the evaluator's own figure in `published`. A literal equal to the shared value is a copy; a literal that differs is the same question answered another way. A place or year the shared facts don't cover is the only reason to keep a different literal, recorded as a waiver with the reason. Labels stand in for meaning: a concept under other words isn't seen.

title: No house constant without a shared fact
how: Input rows on the path to the output (not variants) are grouped by whose figure it is (an evaluator, or charityevals; SoGive's copies of GiveWell's sheets count as GiveWell's), by label (significant words, place names and "overall" dropped) and by value: a group spanning five or more models is a constant copied by hand. It becomes a shared fact (facts/*.json) that every copy reads (GiveWell's: facts/givewell_common.json; our staff-pay defaults: facts/staff_pay.json). Round structural numbers lint allows in formulas (0, 1, 0.5, 100, 1000, 100000, 1000000, 12, 52, 365, 365.25, 0.000001: no adjustment, a hypothetical $1,000, months in a year) aren't house constants, nor is a number that defines its row (an arbitrary or hypothetical donation's size; a scenario whose label states its value, "10x bar" = 10). Rows reading a fact are formulas and never counted; the same number under different labels, or from different evaluators, is a coincidence, not a copy.

title: A ranked model far above its peers says why
how: For every model the rankings use (rankingPlan), at the defaults in our view: if its headline is more than 10× the median of the other ranked models of the same cause (at least three), its summary must state the reason in the words "more than ten times its peers because …". The best guess stays; the outlier is explained where readers meet it.

title: Side sheets never rank; the ranked column is the grant's
how: For every model the rankings use: at most one row on its path may read like a value-of-information or decision sheet (future funding bar, reallocated funding, value of information, the probability a decision changes, P(… x cash)); two or more and the sheet values what a grant lets the funder learn, so it must be a side sheet (src/engine/ranking.ts SIDE_SHEET or VOI_ROW). And where the native row's label ends in a place in parentheses (GiveWell's "Final cost-effectiveness estimate (Chad)"), the model's name, id or source title must name that place too when it names any: otherwise the importer took another location's column.

title: Deaths in WELLBY models don't move with the WELLBY rate
how: WELLBY models (not variants) that value a death (a row on the path reads @moral_weights.* or $life_value_multiplier) must value it in units of value in uov_valued_outside_wellbys and put it into WELLBYs only in wellbys_from_uov = uov_valued_outside_wellbys / ($daly_per_wellby * $uov_per_daly) (in an ours section; INV-2b), which the unit's conversion ($daly_per_wellby * $uov_per_daly) cancels. Checked by computation: the deaths' part of the headline (headline − headline with uov_valued_outside_wellbys = 0) doesn't move when $daly_per_wellby is ×1.5, and the rest (every bridge's input at 0) doesn't move with $life_value_multiplier. Any other model with a bridge from uov (docs/normalization.md 2.6) values its deaths only upstream of that bridge.

title: Past averages, and only past averages, read the next-dollar slider
how: Every model with an output (variants inherit the field) declares estimate_basis. past_average: a row on the path to the output reads $marginal_vs_past_average, halving it lowers our headline, and every row reading it has the evaluator's value in `published` (or the evaluator pins it), so the evaluator view keeps the average. marginal and unit_cost: no row reads $marginal_vs_past_average.

title: An estimate counts less by its age, in our view only
how: Every model with a result in common units (not templates) has source.published. With every model it reads live (`#id`) held at its value at $estimate_age_discount = 0, its headline at the slider's default, at 10% and at its high end equals its headline at 0 times (1 + d)^−age exactly (age from source.published to common.estimate_age_as_of); the evaluator view's headline, destinations included, is the same at every setting.

title: Lives near and far: weighed by where they are, in our view only
how: Every model with a result in common units (not templates) has beneficiaries: shares by ISO 3166 alpha-3 codes in facts/countries.json (and "world", spread by population) summing to 1, "world", or "destinations" when it reads other models live. With $home_country = 0 at a discount of 50% and 90%, and with homes United States, Nigeria, India and the United Kingdom at 0, the headline is exactly its headline with neither. At 50% a step with each of those homes, and the models it reads live held, the headline is its headline with no home times the weight worked out country by country, Σ share × (1 − d)^steps (0 the home country, 1 its UN M49 region, 2 elsewhere; 1 for "destinations", whose destinations bring their own); the evaluator view's headline is the same at every setting.

title: Missing outcome data: one rule for every model, in our view only
how: Every model with a result in common units (not templates) is classified: a charityevals model by its missing_data_adj rows and no missing_data field; an imported one by missing_data (its own or inherited) with a reason and no row reading $missing_data_discount. At $missing_data_discount = 1 an import's factor is exactly 1 and an own build's headline equals its headline with every marker at 1. With the models it reads live held, an import's headline at the default and at 10% is its headline at 1 times 1 − thin_share × (1 − d); the evaluator view's headline is the same at every setting.
